name: Downtime — What Were You Up To?
description:
What a runner got up to between jobs, on their own time. Each player rolls once per downtime period.

2d6, so the quiet middle is common and both extremes are rare (a jackpot or a disaster is about 3%). The mechanical hooks are suggestions — overrule them freely.

results.text: Something bad went down. A deal soured, a fixer sold you out, or the wrong people put your name in a file. Lose one Contact — the GM picks, and they have gone to ground, gone bad, or gone missing — or buy your way clear for [[2d6*500]]¥. Your call, but you decide before you know the price.
A run went bad. You took the job, it fell apart, nobody got paid. No nuyen this downtime, and the lifestyle still comes due. If you cannot cover it, drop a lifestyle level until you can.
You picked up heat. Somebody is asking about you by description. The GM opens the next run with one complication already in play — a tail, a flagged SIN, or a Lone Star patrol that knows your face.
You met someone new. Make a Contact at Loyalty 1 and Connection 1–3; you decide what they do, the GM decides what they want. Roll on Contact Loyalty & Reaction the first time you lean on them.

You put in the work. Training, practice, or a course you actually finished. The Karma cost of your next skill improvement drops by 1 (minimum 1). Name the skill now, before you know what the next run needs.
You laid low. Sleep, cheap soy, bad trid. Nothing gained, nothing lost — and nobody found you either. Clear any heat left over from a previous downtime.
Odd jobs. Bodyguard work, a courier run, a night on a door. No story in it, but the rent is covered: [[1d6*100]]¥ and your lifestyle is paid this month.
You got a line on gear. One item you have been after is available this downtime at −2 to its Availability target number or at a 10% discount — pick one. The offer dies when the next run starts.
A contact came through. One of your Contacts does you a favour unasked: a warning, an introduction, a piece of hardware, or a name you needed. Raise their Loyalty by 1 (max 6).
Things went your way. A debt got paid, a rumour turned out true, or someone owed you and actually remembered. Gain [[1d6*500]]¥ and one straight answer from the GM about an upcoming job.
A spectacular score. You freelanced without the team and it went perfectly. Gain [[1d10*1000]]¥. The GM decides who noticed — that much nuyen moving leaves a trail.
